scope: Optional robust review of named target correspondences; explicit exclusion adoption; existing joint coordinate-constrained solver retained. Complete delivered 0.17.2 features retained.

registration_numeric_checks.scope: Synthetic numerical/API/persistence checks and five retained registration/import/project tests. E57/LAS export-format suite is historical, not rerun by this gate. No field accuracy or native Windows claim.

checks.name: Registration ribbon Join scans opens the optional Review suspect matches step before Solve geometry
Keyboard review runs real exhaustive geometry checks, safely renders target names, and leaves pairs, Check/Exclude roles and measured coordinates unchanged
Review controls remain reachable in short/narrow windows and follow light/dark application themes
Editing pair identity, roles, kept coordinates, tolerance, mode, scan selection or vertical confirmation invalidates the displayed proposal
A suspect kept target is visibly protected, blocks automatic exclusions and retains its Keep selection
An independent Check mismatch is called out immediately and never becomes an automatic exclusion
Too few independent Fit pairs and competing equal-support transformations remain review-only; the normal solver remains available
Real late review responses are discarded after close or Escape and reopening; pending reviews disable editable pairs and Solve
The started review ID is bound to the completed result; a newer real review cannot be mistaken for an older pending response
A late adoption response cannot rewrite rows after its dialog closes and reopens
Stop review cancels the real bounded search, clears the proposal and restores editable controls
The larger named-target set reports actual uniform sampling without inventing a correspondence-quality ranking
A failed review clears prior results and reports an actionable input error
Explicit adoption changes only the two reviewed unkept Fit rows to Exclude; all kept coordinates and independent Check/Exclude choices are preserved
The existing Solve geometry → reviewed Apply geometry workflow still registers and merges the two scans with all three chosen reference coordinates held
No JavaScript errors, failed HTTP requests or injected HTML dialogs in the reviewed registration workflow
Independent disk read confirms merged point count, exact kept coordinates, unchanged original caches and frozen application source

registration_browser.scope: Production algorithms and HTTP in Linux Chromium with generated survey-scale targets and imported XYZ scans. Delayed response checks forward real responses. No real RTC360 data, native Windows UI or 550-million-point performance claim.

installer_transactions.scope: Installer activation checks on Linux. Includes complete preservation and backup of a >20 MB existing project.json, rejection of nonisolated/existing self-check workspaces, and activation refusal on startup-check failure. No native Windows runtime claim.

startup_self_check.fixture_data: Synthetic metadata only; no scan points or user project paths.
startup_self_check.scope: The same oversized-metadata self-check body used before installer activation, executed on Linux with the explicitly recorded validation runtime. Native Windows execution occurs when the installer runs on Windows.

limitations: Linux software/browser/build checks; no native Windows/WebView2 or user-PC installation was executed.

Synthetic correspondence, target and cloud fixtures; the newly described three-setup/three-sphere sample, sphere centre fitting and field millimetre accuracy are not validated. This release does not add automatic sphere recognition.
Review uses at most 200 target matches, not the full 550-million-point cloud; no whole-project runtime or 7 GB RAM guarantee is established by these tests.
Source-preserved historical functionality is not claimed as fully retested. E57/LAS export-format tests were not rerun in this registration update.
Largest observed consensus does not prove physical target identity. Bounded searches can miss alternative solutions; no correctness probability is reported.
The Varga/Laki keypoint+FPFH+FGR paper was assessed as future cloud-registration guidance; no Harris/ISS/FPFH/FGR pipeline or detector change is shipped here.
